utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I want to address a matter that arose in court yesterday and that implicates the issue of protective measures that we discussed somewhat earlier, so I ask to move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Could the Chamber move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Since the issue of third-party statements was raised, probably it's better to deal with now. Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Robinson, in relation to the next witness, I noted that the Defence added 6 paragraphs and 11 associated exhibits. I think if my memories correct, the Defence is planning to tender nine third-party statements as associated exhibits, but to my understanding, it has been the Chamber's practice that it rarely admitted third-party statement as associated exhibits, so it's difficult -- if we allow it, it may be a slippery slope to admit third-party statement through that regime. And it's very difficult for the Chamber to find in what context or in what sense the witness is confirming or commenting on the third-party statement. So if you'd like to tender third-party statement, I would like you, the Defence, to lead live so that the Chamber can assess the relevance and the authentic -- authenticity as well, the veracity of the content through the witness. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I didn't know if the Court was about to move on to call the witness in. I just want a quick notification to raise for the Court. Actually, to some extent implicated by our recent -- or implicates our recent discussion. Yesterday the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Court asked yesterday for advanced notification of objections to documents. In the case of an upcoming witness, Mr. Sarenac, the Prosecution has been reviewing in excess of 200 associated exhibits proposed to be tendered by the Defence. There will be numerous objections to those, but the review of those documents alone has been a time consuming exercise. I believe Ms. Edgerton would be prepared to discuss those in advance, for example, on Monday, but I wanted to alert the Court and -- and the Defence to the fact that such objections were coming, and the Court in particular because it may wish to conduct a preliminary review of those documents since it is an extremely time consuming exercise to get a grip on that voluminous material. So I wanted to let the Court know in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Shall we bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Savkic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Savkic.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just one question: The people who demolished the mosque, were they identified?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They have never been identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the police launch an investigation and try to uncover the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they did, but this was done in such an unprofessional way, because all the windows, around 5 -- 2.500 windows in Vlasenica were demolished, which means that people who set off this explosion obviously didn't know anything about that, and it was generally a disastrous event for the town.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions at this juncture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, by this the Defence is not tendering 1D13045 and 1D13046?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then shall we redact those paragraphs or -- or at least reference to the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We can redact the reference to the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is in paragraph 77.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And so it would be from the word "document" down to the end of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So it's including the -- the additional statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In case of para 77, from "document" until the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And 78?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I think it would have to stop after the word "jihad."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: "Jihad." Make a full stop at "jihad." Do you follow, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then, Mr. Savkic, as you have noted, your evidence in chief has been concluded, most of which was done in writing in lieu of your oral testimony. Then you will be now cross-examined by the Office of the Prosecutor, but before doing so, yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I just noticed as the Court was making its inquiry that the witness was thumbing through a pile of documents. I think that the first -- the one on top is in fact his statement. There were other documents, so I think the witness should be cautioned if he's going to look at and make reference to documents during the course of his testimony he should alert the Court first before looking at those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger, and I will leave it to Ms. Sutherland. So if --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and thank you, Mr. Tieger. Your Honours, forgive me for not seeking leave yesterday to remain seated while I addressed you, and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: By all means, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I seek leave to conduct my examination seated.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, can you -- can you put the -- all the documents that are on the table which are not your statement, can you put them away from the table, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me be clear, Mr. Savkic. It's fine for you to have your statement with you now, but in order to consult other documents, please let us know before you'd like to -- before you see the document. Do you understand that, sir? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do. However, these documents are related to paragraph 78. Yesterday, the lady said that she couldn't see the context out of which an assertion about al-Qaeda was extracted, and because of that, I brought all these three documents that clearly indicate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The reason I asked you to put down the documents is to see whether you are able to answer the question from the top of your head or you have to rely on certain documents. It relates to your credibility, et cetera. Do you understand that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then you are free to look at your statement at any time. Let's continue. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, I have very limited time this morning, so I would ask you to listen to the question and focus on the question and answer the question only. If I need you to elaborate on your answer, then I will ask you a follow-up question. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You previously testified before this Tribunal over five days in January 2006 in the case of Momcilo Krajisnik. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Have you reviewed that transcript at any time since you testified?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes and no. Since it was first translated from Serbian into English and then from English back to Serbian, some sentences make no sense, but I do recall this, that testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, the short answer to that would have been yes. You have reviewed it. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes and no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's continue, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your statement that's just been admitted that you gave to the Defence, when did you provide that statement?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps some ten days ago, and there were some minor changes that were made a couple of days ago. They were more grammatical changes and some clarifications.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When were you first approached by the Defence? When did you first speak to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what you mean by "the Defence," but three or four months ago with Mr. Marko. I don't know. If you're referring to this part of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Marko Sladojevic, the gentleman sitting over there?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Have you spoken to anyone else on the Defence team about your statement? Investigators, other lawyers?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with lawyers, but I did with investigators, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Luka Bogdanovic was his name, Luka Bogdanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, my apologies. Can I interrupt here? I have one thing that I forgot to tell Mr. Karadzic. So we go back to his examination-in-chief. With respect to para 35 and 36, more specifically last sentence of para 35 and -- or para 36, it was unclear to me on what basis the witness had knowledge of -- or could reach that conclusion referred to in these paragraphs, so before Ms. Sutherland continues her cross-examination, I would like to clarify with the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I or you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please. It's your examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Savkic, in your statement you said that Izet Redzic informed Izetbegovic about your negotiations, I think you said negotiations, about an establishment of three municipalities and that Izetbegovic told him to stall as much as possible and to try to lead the Serbs by creating false impressions. How did you find out about that?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was representing the Serb people and Redzic was representing the Muslim people and we were two of the six mean who were involved in reaching that agreement. He was a very talkative person, so I assume that in a conversation with one of his friends, he said that he asked this Mr. Izetbegovic. As for the correspondence between him and Izetbegovic was no secret at all. He was the President of the Executive Board, so all the correspondence could be found in the municipal archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, as for the others, for example, the president of municipality, did he have an insight into that archives?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. President Stanic would have been one of those people, and I would like to add that he is still a good friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 36, it is said that it was in their interest not only to stall the negotiations but to have the Muslims leave Vlasenica, and you said that it had been ordered and that the probable purpose was an attack on Vlasenica. On the basis of what did you reach that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says clearly here that after the joint session of the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica held on the 13th of April, 1992, he and Stanic went after the meeting to Tuzla to try to explain to the refugees and to tell them to come back from Tuzla to Vlasenica. However, after some time, Izet Redzic didn't want to come back, whereas President Stanic returned. In the room where Izet Redzic was working, a log-book was found and there's this famous page dated the 13th of April which clearly indicates, and it's written here and it's been admitted into this court, that he had asked chief of Tuzla municipality, Beslagic, whether these Muslim refugees should remain there temporarily or permanently. So that was an indication of an intention to manipulate these unfortunate refugees. And then in the corner of that page there is one very symptomatic thing, and that is that a professor was asked to take students out of the secondary school centre and to bring a motor and an inductor into the school. All of us who know at least something about warfare and equipment, et cetera, an inductor has only one purpose and one purpose alone, and that is a device that is used to activate explosives. In addition to that, in the bottom right part of that page from his notebook is depicted a clear structure of how the authorities would be taken over in Vlasenica and who should be involved in that, and it is also written that all this operation was to be directed by the General Staff, and that was the document admitted here in this courtroom, and I have documents to that effect.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would this suffice, your Excellencies?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I will leave it at that. Mr. Savkic, you have your statement with you now. Could you take a look at para 34. First sentence reads: "On 31st of March, the municipality of Milic adopted a decision to establish the municipality of Milici. Did you mean to refer to Milic or Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That's a historical fact. The municipality was established at that time, however, it did not start working until the 13th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. My question is whether it relates to Milici or Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This decision as it's written here relates to the municipality of Milici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. Back to you, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, in paragraph 2 of your statement it sets out the positions or functions that you held from when you left school until at the end of the war and it don't mention what functions you held in the SDS party. You stated in cross-examination in the Krajisnik case that in late 1991 or the beginning of 1992, you took over the functions of the president of the SDS party in Vlasenica. That is the municipal board of Vlasenica, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the Municipal Board in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the reference to the transcript was 20634 to 20635. You also said you were a member of the Municipal Board of the SDS in Milici from 1993 until -- until the present time, which was the date you were testifying in -- in Krajisnik, and that you were also a member of the Main Board from 2001 to 2005. And that's at transcript page 20635 to 20636. Are you still a member of the SDS today?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You were also a member of the Serbian Autonomous District of Birac Assembly, yes?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only attended its sessions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In the Krajisnik trial you were shown some documents relevant to the SAO Birac. You stated that the meetings of the Assembly of SAO Birac were held but the Executive Council of -- was never fully functioned and that the Birac SAO region never existed as such and that was at transcript pages 20664 to 20665. I'd like to call up a document, 65 ter number 17438A, please. If we could go to page 4 in the e-court and page 17 in the English translation. This is minutes of the 5th of February of the meeting of the Assembly of the autonomous district Birac held on the 5th of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, I was checking. It's only seven pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, Your Honour. I'm --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You were shown this document. It says here that you're appointed as a member of the political council. Do you see that? It's on page 7 of the English translation. I'm sorry. And it's on page 4 of the B/C/S. Mr. Savkic, we can see from the first page of this document that this meeting was -- took place in Milici. Do you agree with me that you were a member of this political council? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see anything. All I can see is page 31.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can we please go to page 4 of the B/C/S. I'm sorry. Could we go to page 3 of the English then. It doesn't appear to be the B/C/S document. Could we go to page 7 of the English translation. The previous page, page 6. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you see here down the bottom and I will have it translated for you, the members elected to the political council, 1, Jovo Mijatovic from Zvornik; 2, Miroslav Deronjic from Bratunac; 3, Miroslav Stanic from Kladanj. The following page: 4 is Zdravko Vukovic from Kladanj; 5 Tomislav Savkic from Milici/Vlasenica, and then it continues another --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have B/C/S page. Let's show him the previous page, page 6. The next page. Yes, please continue, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you see there that you are -- this is a meeting held in Milici on the 5th of February, 1992, and it states that you are a member of the political council? Were you a member of this council? Is it your position today -- what is your position today?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that I attended the Assembly of the autonomous region, the only one that was held, and that was on the 8th of January in Sekovici. In the Krajisnik trial, a commission with a totally different name was put to me that had been elected by the government at that one meeting held in Sekovici, and on that occasion, I said that some of those people I had never seen in my life before, and I am sure that it must have been recorded in the transcript, because I recall it clearly. Now what you're talking about, the 5th of February --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry. I will show you that document now. If I can have 65 ter number 17442. These are the minutes of the first session of the Executive Council of the Birac SAO, dated the 18th of February, 1992. And on page 2 of the English, it says that you were appointed a member of a four-member team of representatives of the region tasked to review the existing map of the ethnic region. And in the Krajisnik trial, you said it's difficult for a man to remember all the details when you were asked about your membership of this four-man team, and you said you were never consulted by anyone as to whether you would be a member, and that was at transcript page 20666 to 20667.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now that you've had some time to reflect on the matter, do you now agree that you were participated in councils and teams dealing with political and ethnic issues in the region?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Even the minutes that you're showing me now, I don't remember it at all. I don't know. I think it's not clear to me. Well, not exactly not clear to me, but quite simply those were working bodies that had no particular function. As I said, for example, this person listed under number 4 is someone who is completely unknown to me. I can take another look at the minutes of the meeting, but this is first that I am looking at it at this meeting or minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is not the first time you've seen this document. It was shown to you in the Krajisnik trial -- I'm sorry, Mr. Karadzic. I will move on, Mr. Savkic. In paragraph 34 of your statement, you state that the Milici municipal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I take it you are not tendering these documents, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you are, I'd like to deal with it one by one. Yes, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I don't see well, but could I please be assisted. Where does is say here that among the attendees we can see Mr. Savkic? In the second paragraph we have Radojlub Djukanovic, Goran Zekic, Milan Miljanovic [phoen], and Vuk Hajlovic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's on page 2. Four-member team. The memberships are Jovo Miskin and the four-member team were Tomo Savkic from Milici, Rajko Vidakovic from Sekovici, Mitar Tesic from Bratunac and Nego Jovtic from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. The conclusion is dealing with the formation or appointment. Mr. Karadzic's point was -- point was whether the witness was present in this meeting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Savkic, what did you say?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly was not there. I mean, there's no need to check.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Regardless of whether you attended the meeting, you were -- you were put onto a four-member team. My question was now that you've had time to reflect over the past six years, do you now agree that you participated in councils and teams dealing with political and ethnic issues in the region, in the SAO Birac region?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This commission --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Savkic. It requires a yes or no answer. What is your position today?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this commission. Well -- well, you know, you may be asking for a yes or no. I mean, if somebody has a particular kind of education, then one has to know how to analyse this. This commission never met. The question is whether this decision was ever made and submitted to these four persons. I believe that that did not happen. Now, as far as this other work is concerned --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] I showed you two documents where -- where you are listed as -- as being involved. I asked you what your position was, whether you were in fact dealing with matters to do with political and ethnic issues in the region. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to move on now to paragraph 34 of your --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, I seek to tender those two documents, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Turning first to 17438A, if you could look at that document at the very beginning of the document, the first two paragraphs. I question the provenance of this document in light of those paragraphs. Also, although the witness didn't confirm anything about the document, I don't think it also is reliable enough to be said to directly contradict him, so we are imposing the admission of that document. With respect to the other document, 17442, I think it goes to the weight, and we will not object to its admissibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Could you explain to us, Ms. Sutherland, about the provenance? It says "excerpts from Srebrenica."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will have to get back to you in relation to the provenance of this document. I would be happy to redact that top portion of what appears in the document and starting simply with the minutes, but I will get back to the Court in relation to the provenance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So this is not a proper minute but the minute contained in a book.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It appears so, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So what do you suggest with respect to this document at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We can MFI it until I get back to the Court in relation to the provenance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But -- yes, to be sure, Mr. Savkic you confirm you attended that meeting in Milici in February.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no, no, no. This is the first time I see the minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we show him the first page and -- first page first. 17438A. It says the -- there's a meeting, meeting held -- no, no. I'm talking about 17 -- yes. I'm correct. Meeting held in Milici on 5th of February. Shall we show him the next page? Next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can assist. On page 4 of the English translation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, but page 3, probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic is speaking at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That's the point I wanted to show him. Do you find that, sir? Where is the -- let me find the B/C/S page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, at page 4 in B/C/S as well. Here it is noted that you held that this area and its economy should be connected to Serbia, and its economy Western Serbia, in particular. You think the programme should be adopted. Do you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember this, although the words are very affirmative. I don't remember this meeting at all, because I was not a member of that Assembly. That's a very important thing. And that can be seen from the first page. It is possible in terms of good husbandry that I sometimes did enter that Assembly because it was open, so I may have sort of walked in, but I do not rule out that possibility. I walked in, greeted all those people, but it is certain that I was not a member of the Assembly of the SAO Birac. Everyone knows full well who the 15 members from Vlasenica were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And you would not deny that you were elected as member of the political council, as you saw earlier on in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've told you I deny that because I never received that decision. Well, I wouldn't have minded to work that political body had I known in view of the names of these persons. The times were the way they were. These decisions were never distributed to anyone except for -- well, this is the first time I see the minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me -- show the page 6. I was talking about this council, political council.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do know these people, but no, no, no. Never. No. As a matter of fact, for example, Zdravko Vukovic, never heard of him. Miroslav from Kladanj, never heard of him. I doubt it. At any rate, this political council never met, although it had ben established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI P6112, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the next one. Did we give the number for that?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 017442 will be P6113, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, in paragraph 34 of your statement you said that the Milici municipality -- municipal Assembly was established on the 31st of March, 1992. When you testified in the Krajisnik case, you said that no decisions were taken at the republic level by the Assembly to proclaim the municipality of Milici, and that's at transcript page 20653. You were shown the minutes of the 24th of March, 1992, meeting of the 12th session of the Assembly of the Serbian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina, where the Assembly verified the proclamation of the Serbian municipality of Milici. The minutes that you were shown make it clear that a decision was taken by the republic level in relation to the proclamation, and you -- you would agree with that proposition now?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree. A Serb municipality of Milici was never proclaimed. Even this Assembly that was held on the 31st of March, 1992, where it is clearly stated that that is the municipality of Milici without any prefix of Serbian, even that was held without us knowing about it, us who had negotiated the territorial distribution of the municipality of Vlasenica. And now this Assembly that you've been talking about, I can guarantee that all of us negotiators there, both Muslims and Serbs, and I mean I don't know who it was that proposed this anyway, because this was not in the interest of the population of Milici or the population of Vlasenica, either Serb or Muslim. There was no need for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll move on. It's Exhibit P00961. It's at page 23 of the English translation and at page 41 of the B/C/S where the RS Assembly verifies the proclamation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, in paragraph 46 of your statement you state that there was no Crisis Staff in Milici. Your position is that it never functioned. It was never established. It never functioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I can have 65 ter number 5 -- 00571, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is dated the -- this is a Serbian municipality of Milici Crisis Staff decision numbered 005/5, and it's about directing of taxes on the turnover of goods and services, and we see here a signature block, President of Crisis Staff, Tomislav Savkic. You were shown this document in Krajisnik, and you made an unsubstantiated claim that the document was a forgery and this is at transcript page 20775. We can see at the top of the document a stamp with the municipal administration receiving the document, and we see a stamp at the bottom of the document, Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you still -- is it still your position that this document is a forgery?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claimed that then, and the Chamber of this Court --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- confirmed that I was 100 per cent right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I have limited time. It required a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I think the witness has to be given a chance to give an explanation even if he gives yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have very limited time and I think the witness could answer a your or a no; and if I want him to elaborate he can, or if Mr. Karadzic would like him to further elaborate he can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: "I claimed then" and now -- "confirmed that I was a 100 per cent right." I think we can leave it there. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I -- I don't see where it is written, the Serb municipality of Milici, as Madam Sutherland said on page 29, line 21. And the witness was trying to say it was the Trial Chamber that said that he was right.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went into closed session and said I was right. I can tell you. I can explain. It's the stamp that is a forgery. I showed it to the Court at that point in time. I have all of it here. All of it was forged because of the taxes that the Boksit company wanted to keep for themselves, and that's why I didn't want to sign this. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, this document shows that there is a Milici Crisis Staff established and functioning and that you are the president of the Milici Crisis Staff. Do you deny that?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Everyone understand that this never existed in Milici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I didn't hear you, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I seek to tender this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. Unless we have more evidence of its provenance, the witness has -- well, it contradicts the witness. There's no showing of the reliability of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will -- if we can mark it for identification, I will provide the Court with the provenance of this document. May I move on, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not only the provenance but also the authenticity probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI P6114, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: May I have 65 ter number 00569, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, so you're saying that the Milici Crisis Staff wasn't in existence and that you weren't the president. This is a document dated the 27th of May, 1992. It's a report of the duty officer of the commander of the Milici police station, and it refers to the fact that the Milici Crisis Staff was informed of an attack on a convoy. You were also shown this document in Krajisnik, and you stated that it was possible that the author had merely mistakenly referred to the military authority as the Crisis Staff, and that's at transcript page 20676. Having seen this document is it -- is it still your position that you were -- that there was no Milici Crisis Staff in operation?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is called the Crisis Staff of Milici is actually the communications centre at the miners' hall. So absolutely there was no Crisis Staff in Milici. This was the communications centre where people came and reported what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6115, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can have 65 ter number 00572, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, this is a decision on the discontinuation of the Crisis Staff of -- of the Milici municipality which is being replaced by the military command and the wartime Presidency. You were also shown this document in -- in Krajisnik. You conceded that this decision was based on a republic-level decision to abolish Crisis Staffs. However, you maintained that the Crisis Staff had in fact not functioned, and that was at transcript page 20673. Upon reflection and seeing these documents again, one where the Crisis Staff is issuing a decision, another where the SJB are reporting to the Crisis Staff and another where the Crisis Staff is being abolished pursuant to a decision of the Serb leadership, does this change your mind as to the fact that you were the president of the Milici Crisis Staff which was in existence from March until the end of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document and three or four other documents were shown to me before that court, and I said about all of them why they were forged and how and who forged them. If I need to repeat that here to you now, I can do that no problem whatsoever. I can explain that to this Court and any other court. I remember those documents very well, five or six of them. They were all forged in the later period in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. In light of the witness's comments, I think it should be MFI'd for a further showing of authenticity and reliability.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What does the first sentence mean, Article 1? It has been become discontinued by then or it has been discontinued till then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, on the face of the document, it appears to be in the past tense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Does it mean it was not in existence?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No. It was in existence and it's been discontinued. It's being -- it's being abolished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we -- or actually, maybe I can do that too. Could we ask the witness to explain the preamble, because the preamble is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Just a second. It's up to you to take up the issue in your redirect. Would you like to add anything to the authenticity of this document, Ms. Sutherland or are you happy to mark it for identification?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can mark it for identification at the moment. It -- it does have the stamp at the bottom of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But you didn't ask the witness about the signature and the name -- the person named Mile Lalovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, do you know Mr. Lalovic?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I think -- [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: He was a -- he was a friend of yours? He was an acquaintance of yours? That's his signature?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's the man who forged all of those documents in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, it just occurred to me have these documents been admitted in the Krajisnik case? If they have been you can probably admit them on their reliability not the authenticity under Rule 94, but if they haven't been, then we would maintain our objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, they have. 65 ter number 00571 was Krajisnik Exhibit P1055. 65 ter number 00569 was Krajisnik Exhibit P1057, and 65 ter number 00572 was Krajisnik Exhibit P1056. I thank you, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, the witness has testified that this was formed by Mile Lalovic. Upon that basis, we can admit it and it will go to the weight. So we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6116, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, War Presidencies replaced the Crisis Staffs, and they performed the functions of the Municipal Assembly, yes?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this specific case as far as Milici's concerned, no. As far as I know, that is. Because the Municipal Assembly of Milici and the Executive Board of Milici worked throughout this period from the 13th of April, 1992, and further on. Now, whether they established a war Presidency or not, you should ask Mile Lalovic, in that period, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter number 00585.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, this is a document, a report dated the 8th of December, 1992. It's a report on the expanded session of the Milici municipality War Presidency, and it's addressed to the -- Milan Zivanovic, commander the Drina Corps. And if we can go over the page of the English translation. It says here that -- sorry. If we can go back to page 1. It says here that the Milici municipality War Presidency which has the function of the Municipal Assembly. So right the way through 1992, it was performing the functions of the Municipal Assembly. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I do not agree. If you prepared this here, then you could have prepared records of all the sessions of the Assembly of Milici and all sessions of the Executive Board. Now, this is what I'm asking you: This War Presidency, if somebody was president of the Crisis Staff, how come that that man who's president of the Crisis Staff is not on the War Presidency? And I happen to be that particular person. Is there any logic there?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Savkic, I'm -- I'm the one that's asking you the questions. We can go -- could we go to the back page, please.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to the last page. We can see that the signature block is the War Presidency. It has a stamp, and it's sent to the Drina Corps command, the Birac Brigade command, and the Milici Municipal Assembly. My question -- my earlier question was that these War Presidencies and in Milici performed the functions of the Municipal Assembly right through 1992; is that right? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I think my position is the same that in light of the witness's response there is a question about authenticity and reliability but if it's been admitted in the Krajisnik case we wouldn't object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the witness is saying that this is forged or it was written by Lalovic but he does not agree with the content of it. Can you assist us, Mr. Savkic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which document do you have in mind, this one or the ones I've referred to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This -- I mean this one, Mr. Savkic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bravo. Bravo. You see? Look at the stamp from December. That's the stamp that was used then and then have a look at the previous documents and their stamp. You see, that's why I said that. The stamp was forged, not this one. This is the original, the original stamp of the municipal Assembly of Milici with the coat of arms and the other one, you see, just look at it. It's illogical that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, I'm asking about this document. So this is a genuine document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6117, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document is possibly not forged, although I haven't read all of it. In all likelihood, it is not a forgery, and I know about this period, and I know that the War Presidency sat at the time rather than the Municipal Assembly and its Executive Board. There was a very serious rift at the time in December and January the next year. It was fighting the Cerani Detachment. I know why it was that it is the War Presidency here, because there was no one here who could sit. I thought the president asked me about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will take a break now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we will resume at 4 past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, very briefly before I do, can I make a submission to you? I was granted one and a half hours with this witness, and I've taken 45 minutes of that time already. I initially had asked for two and a half hours which I didn't think was unreasonable given that his statement is 99 paragraphs covering both 1992 and 1995 issues. I have nine discrete issues relating to 1992 to go, and I then have six discrete issues in relation to Srebrenica, but I have quite a number of relevant and probative documents to put to the witness which I think will take some time. Up until this point it's been incredibly slow with the documents in e-court for a number of reasons, and so I am asking if I could have some additional time to do that with these -- to cover the issues that I have flagged to deal with with the next witness. And if I can just say with the next witness I don't envisage taking 45 minutes with cross-examination and that's what I say at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It would be pretty much to set a specific period of time at this moment, but all I can say is to try your best and see how it evolves. Let's continue, Ms. -- it's noted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you were also president of the Milici War Presidency established in 1995, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if we can see 65 ter number 02373, please. This is a War Presidency situation report to the Republika Srpska Ministry of Defence on the situation in the Milici municipality, and I think it's signed by you as president of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this is you reporting on the situation at -- at the time?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6118, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You received orders and sought instructions from the central state organs, and you consulted with Mr. Karadzic for his approval of proposed War Presidency members, didn't you? Not in relation to this document, Mr. Savkic. It's a proposition I'm putting to you, that you received orders and sought instructions from the central state organs, including Mr. Karadzic. You consulted with him for his approval on War Presidency members. Is that -- that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of all War Presidencies --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter number 17320. Are you saying that you didn't consult with Mr. Karadzic to seek his approval on the proposed War Presidency members? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. For all municipalities after Srebrenica and Krajina fell, instructions were issued on the establishment of War Presidencies. It was nothing special for Milici. It involved all of the municipalities. Instructions were provided on how to establish War Presidencies. That's how it was. Nothing special. There was no personal contact or anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But we see here this document in front of us your proposal for the formation of the War Presidency of the municipality of Milici. This is signed by you. If we could move the document up a little. And this is where you're writing to Mr. Karadzic, attention personally seeking -- listing the proposed members. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever is on this paper is something that I signed as the speaker of the Municipal Assembly. It was my proposal. There's nothing to dispute in here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I seek to tender this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6119, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can have 65 ter 01693.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is an Official Gazette of the Republika Srpska dated the 28th of August, 1995, and if we can have 01693A. I'm sorry. And this is Mr. Karadzic's decision on the establishment of the War Presidency in 1995, is it not? Mr. Savkic?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's nothing to say. What do you expect me to say? Perhaps it's not the same as I had proposed. I don't know. I'm not sure what you're looking for.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm not giving evidence from the bar table but if we compare the two documents you will see that the names are the same as those that you proposed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I seek to tender this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6120, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic I want to now turn your attention back to 1992. In paragraph 37, you state that talking about Vlasenica town you state that, It was agreed that we should go into town with our units, and this is on the 20th and 21st of April, 1992. When you say it was agreed that we should go into town, it was agreed by whom, the Crisis Staff? Or the Crisis Staff and the military?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was the paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thirty-seven.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thirty-seven. This is what -- the language of what's his name, Luka Bogdanovic. It says that it was agreed. It referred to the command of the 216th wartime Mountain Brigade and its battalion, and the arrangement was probably also reached with members of the TO in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When you say this is the language of what's his name, Luka Bogdanovic, you're talking about the Defence investigator?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Defence investigator, yes. It was agreed upon. A decision was made. That was the sense of it, the meaning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It was agreed by who you should go into town? Who was doing the agreeing, the Crisis Staff and the military or who?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's already up there in Vlasenica. I think it was agreed between the command of the battalion of the 216th Brigade and the TO staff, since it was a purely military operation. It had a very clear goal of securing public buildings and institutions. I can't say who participated in it though.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can see Exhibit -- Exhibit 23 -- sorry, 2636, please. So the take-over was conducted by forces of the JNA and the -- and it was co-ordinated by the SDS Crisis Staff. Do you agree? Mr. Savkic?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me have a look first.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Will you look at the document. I'd like you to answer my question. Do you -- I'm saying -- I'm putting to you that the take-over the Vlasenica was conducted by the forces of the JNA and it was co-ordinated by the SDS Crisis Staff. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not co-ordinated by the Crisis Staff. As for the JNA forces, yes, they did enter, and they did the job without a single shot being fired.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We see here this document, P2636. It was a report of the 1st Vlasenica Light Infantry Brigade commander, Mile Kosoric, and it sets out that on the 20th of April the forces of the Yugoslav Army and the -- and the formed unit co-ordinated by the SDS Crisis Staff liberated the town of Vlasenica. This Mile Kosoric was your superior officer, was he not, when you became commander of the Infantry Battalion in later 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mile Kosoric was the commander of the 1st Milici-Vlasenica Brigade that was founded -- well, the date in here is not correct. It was established on the 16th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until then.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your answer is not responsive to my question. I asked if you simply -- if this man, Mr. Kosoric, was your superior officer when you later became commander of the infantry -- Milici Infantry Battalion in late 1992. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was, but only then.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In paragraph 38 of your statement you said that you believe that the Serbian leadership issued a decision on the establishment of the Vlasenica Crisis Staff on the 24th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, Ms. Sutherland. Your previous question, line from 24 page 42, you read out certain paragraph from the document, and at -- in the end you asked whether Kosoric, or Kosoric was his superior, and you didn't give him the opportunity to comment on your other part of your question. So bear that in mind. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- I was simply putting the document to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Putting the document, and you didn't ask a question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But I put the question at line 17. I put it to you that the take-over was conducted by the JNA and the Crisis Staff and he said no it wasn't, and then I put the document to him showing that it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And whether he was his superior.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then I went to ask him about Kosoric. But I'll bear your point in mind, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, would you like to add anything, Mr. Savkic, with respect to document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. It's very simple. All of these assertions provided by Mile Kosoric, that is to say the first paragraph, the second paragraph, the third, the fourth, all the way up to the fifth paragraph. Well, Mile Kosoric was not in Vlasenica at all. Together with his family, he went to Belgrade via Croatia, and he arrived in the area of Vlasenica in September 1992, and it is probably something that the Prosecution's aware of. So all of this is being stated by someone who at the time was not in the territory of Vlasenica municipality at all. Next, he's lying -- or actually not telling the truth in paragraph 4 about some detachments in the field. He made these assertions, I don't know under whose instruction, perhaps by the Prosecution. He says the detachment is still co-ordinated by the Crisis Staff of the SDS, although all of the detachments had been resubordinated to the 1st Bircani Brigade which was established on the day the JNA left, which is the 19th of May. Kosoric is not tell the truth in paragraph 5. That's as clear as day. The brigade was not formed on the 16th of January, 1993, but on the 16th of September. I took over the battalion on the 1st of January, 1992, and it was only because the tragedy at Podravanje on the 24th of September happened, just before that, and I was unable to return to Milici before the 1st of November. The probably only thing that is correct is paragraph 4 when he discusses how the 1st Milici-Vlasenica brigade was split into the Milici and the Vlasenica unit. I think the dates tally. Everything else, save for the third paragraph which says that the 1st Bircani Brigade was formed on the 19th of May, everything else is a lie. It's clear to anyone. This man was describing something while not being present in Bosnia-Herzegovina at all. And I also know why he wrote it, what the problems were, and so on and so forth, but you are perhaps not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 7, is it the 1st of January 1993 or the 1st of September, 1992? There is something that's unclear regarding the date in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may. I was going to bring up the same issue in relation to line 7. The 1st of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you took over the battalion on the 1st of November, 1992, did you not?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, before we went back to that document, I took you to paragraph 38 of your statement where you said that you believed that the Vlasenica Crisis Staff was established on the 24th of April, 1992. You actually amended this in the final version of your statement. You did have the 4th of April in the earlier draft. It is, in fact, the 4th of April that the Crisis Staff was established, wasn't it? And if we can look at 65 ter 23114, this may refresh your memory. Now, if we can just go down to the bottom of the B/C/S first. We can see here that it's got a signature block of Tomislav Savkic, but in fact it's been signed on your behalf. Who -- who -- do you recognise the signature that's below your -- the type-signed name of -- of your?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. On the 4th of April, I have it somewhere in one of the paragraphs here. I was in Tuzla then--

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, in paragraph 38.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to explain. It says the 4th of April. That's why my signature is not there. As for my paragraphs, there is somewhere where it says that on the 4th of April, 1992, I was in Tuzla. I went to see Djeneral Jankovic. But there's nothing to be disputed. The 4th of April. You know that it is basically the beginning of the war. Let's be clear. The Crisis Staffs were formed whenever the situation was critical for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- the people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic. Could you concentrate on answer the question. You stated in your document, in your statement, that it was on 24th of April. Then now Ms. Sutherland was asking whether it was 4th of April. The question could have been much simply -- much more simply answered. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I seek to tender this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6121, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you tender the Kosoric document as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's already an exhibit, P02636.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you didn't answer the question as to if you can recognise the signature below your -- the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we zoom in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No way. This doesn't mean anything to me. I have no idea who may have signed it. It is an unknown signature to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can we just go to the top of the document, please. Now, you see here the predicate paragraph. If we go -- if we can move the English up as well. Following the instructs from the Main Board of the BH SDS regarding operation under conditions of imminent threat of war, the Municipal Board at its session established the Crisis Staff -- made the following decision in establishing the Crisis Staff. These instructions from the Main Board in paragraph 31 of your statement, you said you're not aware of any instructions issued by Karadzic to representatives of municipalities on the 20th of December, 1991, and that you do not know about variants of plans A and B.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not until 2005. Here during a trial that's when I saw the document for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You stated that in Krajisnik. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And in fact in Krajisnik when you said that, you were shown minutes from Assembly sessions that you attended where variant A and B language was used to describe the instructions issued by the SDS Main Board in December 1991. You confirmed in the Krajisnik trial that you were present at the 46th session held in November 1994, which is Exhibit P00401, where Mr. Karadzic stated: "Do you remember the instruction A and instruction B? We had Crisis Staffs," and so on. And you were -- confirmed that -- you were also shown Exhibit P00970 which is a transcript of the 50th session held Sanski Most in April 1995. Again you confirmed that you were present, didn't you? That -- that's correct, isn't that you confirmed in the Krajisnik case that you were present at that session?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Keep quoting what I said in that case so that I don't have to repeat, since you want to quote.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] [Previous translation continues] ... do you agree with me that you were present at the 50th session, yes?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I was present at the session. I also added that I didn't hear about it then either, because I may have left the session, was not in the meeting room. And even if --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the president did tell me --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- what you said was despite these references, and this is at 20722, you stayed that you'd never heard of this instruction and that it wouldn't have meant anything to the uninitiated listener. And you mentioned a moment ago that you -- you said that you may have -- you didn't hear it or you may have left the session, but that's in relation to the trajectory goals which we'll move on to in just a moment.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's what it pertained to, and it is in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the transcript quoted by Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The transcript where he said he was present at the 46 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The witness isn't disputing it. Do we need the transcript pages? Transcript pages where he says he's present at the 46th session is 20 -- 20722 to 20723, transcript pages where he confirmed he was present at the 50th session was 20723 through to 20725, this discussion about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I don't think that that is in dispute. What is disputable is the relation between document A and document B. Did this witness confirm that he had been aware of that document? Can that reference be found in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic can take this matter up in re-examination if he wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And please do not overlap. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you stated in the Krajisnik trial that the first time you saw the strategic goals written down, and this is at transcript page 20713, was when you arrived in The Hague, and that the first time you were made aware of the strategic goals under the heading "Strategic goals," was also when you arrived, and that's at 20618. You stated that you were not aware of the goals in the broad sense, although goals such as strategic goal number 2 you knew about. However, nobody called this a strategic goal. That's at 20618. You said you would rather call it a doctrine or maybe tactical objectives, quote unquote, and that's at 20719. You said that the first time you'd heard of the strategic goals was before Dayton in 1995. And you said that at 20713 to 20714. However, you were present in Assembly sessions when the strategic goals were discussed, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not a deputy at all at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I was not the deputy when they were adopted. Let me correct myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Before we go on, I just put to you a number of transcript references in Krajisnik. You recall saying all of that that I just put to you, do you not? About the fact that you would call it a doctrine, maybe tactical objectives, the first time that you saw it written down was when you came to The Hague. All of that that I just put to you, you remember you said that in the Krajisnik trial, yes?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I cannot remember every word, but I do recall that in the Krajisnik trial I saw the strategic goals in writing for the first time upon my arrival in The Hague in 2006. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But you had heard about it before from Assembly sessions that you had attended, had you not?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: None of us had ever spoken about strategic goals, this or that. Do you understand? Those were a well-educated people, and I'm not quite sure if many of them had never seen it either, just like I never saw it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you said -- you said that you weren't a deputy until later. You became a deputy in mid-1992. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I became a deputy sometime. I know that this - what's it called? - oath that I gave at the Assembly session held in Prijedor. It may have been in August, September, or October. However, I attended the first session before I gave my oath, and I didn't have the right to cast a ballot. But in those three key months, June, July, and August, during the fighting it is well known that I was a commander, and due to that I was prevented from attending sessions. And I also mentioned that in my testimony, and it can also be discerned from the minutes of the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, I'm interested in the Assembly sessions that you did attend. You attended the 34th session.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means nothing to me if you don't tell me the venue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The 34th session was -- was -- was on the 29th of September, 1st of October, 1993, and -- and at that session, Mr. Krajisnik spoke of the strategic goals, and this was shown to you in the Krajisnik case, and this is where you said you'd never heard about it, about the strategic objectives under the heading "Strategic Objectives": "But the matters contained in them I did hear about. I would rather call it a doctrine or maybe tactical objectives. As an officer, I would call them tactical." And that's at transcript page 20719. Do you remember -- you stated that? Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was my comment once I saw the original text of the strategic goals, and of course as a trained officers -- officer, many of those who called those goals strategic goals were people who were well educated, but those were simple tactical objectives; for example, open a corridor. That could not have been strategic goals at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You could have said simply, "Yes," to this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You were also taken to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just wait for the translation. Yes. Do you understand that, sir, Mr. Savkic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I'm not sure I quite understand the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could answer simply by yes and no, please do so. Yes, please continue, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You were also taken to the 36th session which was held on the 30th and 31st of December, 1993. And this was where you were -- you were speaking at this session about your nomination to a council which I'm not going to get into, but you said at the beginning of the war -- sorry. You were referred to paragraphs -- pages 12 to 13 where Mr. Krajisnik begins, and he said at the beginning of the war the Assembly endorsed as one of the most important documents the strategic objectives of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina and organised the people to implement them, and then he enumerated the six strategic object difficulties and you responded that in the work of the Assembly session since it's very long and it happens frequently that deputies leave before the end because of their obligations, and if Mr. Krajisnik did indeed say this at the -- this session, then it's probably at a time when you weren't present and you said that at transcript page 20717 to 20718. However, Mr. Krajisnik spoke at the beginning of the session in relation to the six strategic objectives, and that is he spoke at the session before you did. So in fact, you were in attendance at the session when these strategic objectives were enumerated by Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said of that occasion again that I wasn't present. Now, whether that was in the beginning or in the middle, very often the Assembly worked in commissions, and sometimes it would happen that the commission on which I was, the commission for appointments, was supposed to prepare certain proposals, and it could have happened that we were in a different room at that time. So attendance during a session is immaterial. I attended every session wearing uniform and carrying my weapon, but whether I was late or not late, and the quorum was established maybe on that day or the following day after the session was over. Anyway, if we are talking about strategic goals, I am not a stupid or an insane person to say that this was never discussed. Now, as for the --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- professional meaning of the strategic goals, I gave my opinion at the last --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I want to move on. I've got a couple of -- a few more topics before we get on to the Srebrenica paragraphs of your statement which are about 25 paragraphs in number. In paragraph 36, you state that there can be no talk of expulsions of Muslims from Vlasenica municipality and that it was a SDA plan for them to move out, but, in fact, the moving out of -- or Muslims moving out of the municipality was discussed by the government of the SAO Birac, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a member of the SAO Birac government, but it never existed, in fact. There was only the Autonomous Region of Birac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And in fact, there was an article published in "Javnost," and this is Exhibit P06030 on the 6th of June, 1992, which was setting out a decision of the SAO Birac government regulating the moving out of the Muslim population. Do you recall being confronted with this exhibit in Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I'd like to see it. If I saw it, I might recognise it and then tell you if I had seen it before or not. Show it to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: P06030, please. Now, you see here the government was -- did issue a decision according to this "Javnost" article in relation -- in relation to the safe moving of Muslims from that area.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember reading this, but I find many things to be illogical.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. If you --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to interpret them. You can't see who the author is, but you can see quite clearly that this was not the position of the government but a poetic licence that the author took and obviously since he's using the term "autonomous region," obviously the author is not properly informed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. I will move on to another topic, Mr. Savkic. In -- if we could have Exhibit -- sorry, 65 ter number 00570, please. This is a document dated the 31st of May, 1992. It's a report to the commander of the Milici police station recording that Savkic, Toma, Toma Savkic, was transported by M. Milosevic on the 31st of May, 1992. This M. Milosevic, is that Milomir Milosevic who was stationed at the Milici police station?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this same person was a subordinate of Rade Bjelanovic, the chief of the SJB, Milici SJB?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was his subordinate.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I seek to tender this document, Your Honour.
