utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P6122, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, at paragraphs 63 to 65 of your statement you discuss the Zaklopaca massacre and you say that this attack on the 16th of May, 1992, was fortuitous and it was not planned and it was not a planned and intentional operation. You said that the JNA troops were passing through, and they rested there and heard about some Serbs being killed, and you said that it was basically a revenge attack by foreign troops, and by "foreign" you meant that they are not from Milici. And you said that this is attested to by the fact that "they shot at Serbian houses, too, because they did not know that these were not Muslim houses." How is it then that the only victims that day were over 60 Muslims?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. Which paragraph did you read from?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sixty-three, 64, and 65.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sixty-five, what you asked me about, it is very precisely quoted that the village of Zaklopaca was populated by Serbs and Muslims, and the majority, not all of them, from the group that attacked the village was -- were foreigners or strangers, people who were not from Milici. It was also said that they were shooting at Serb houses, not knowing that those were not Muslim houses. So this is --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, I'm sorry to interrupt you, but if this wasn't a planned and intentional operation how then is it that all the victims that day were all of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next witness will be the best-placed person, Bozidar Trisic to give you this explanation, who was shooting, how the shooting was done and how it all looked like. So instead of me giving an account of what he personally experienced, let him talk about it. And if he hadn't been there to return fire at this shooting, because Serbs were in Zaklopaca, maybe both Serbs and Muslims would have been killed. As far as I remember the words of Bozidar Trisic, there was not a single victim on the Muslim or the Serb side, and those who were shooting from the other side of the street, they killed a Muslim, and his name is known, but equally Djuric could not --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please wait for the interpretation to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Because you were overlapping you were not heard. Not only you, but also the last part of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The end of the answer referred to Djuric and what could have happened to me, so I'm sorry could you please finish.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how far it went on. Which part do I have to repeat? This part where Bozidar Trisic lived, the population was completely mixed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. You said -- you said, "They killed a Muslim, and his name is known, but equally Djuric could not," and later it was not noted. What did you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If Djuric had been there, the owner, the Serb owner of the house, he would have been killed as well. That's one thing. Secondly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- there was a man called Vasiljevic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 3 it doesn't say that the witness said that he had heard that from Trisic. That is where you can see later that Bozidar Trisic -- I mean, it's empty. But what it's supposed to say there is that he heard about these developments from Trisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When did you last speak with Mr. Trisic?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe not less than 10 days or so. I think it's been about 10 days or so. Maybe more. Maybe longer. How long have I been here now, seven, eight days? So maybe it's 15 days. I mean, I talked to him several times. Let's be quite clear on that. I mean for years. This is a man who was born in the village that is right next to my village.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. You testified in the Krajisnik case that you were aware that IPTF had investigated the killing of over 60 Muslim men in Zaklopaca on the 16th of May, 1992, and you agreed that the IPTF concluded that Milomir Milosevic from the Milici SJB had a role in the massacre and that he was suspended from service as a result. You -- you recall saying that at transcript pages 20734 to 20735?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you say that once again? I didn't really hear the first part.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In the Krajisnik case and this is at transcript pages 20734 to 27035, you testified that you were aware that IPTF had investigated the killing of over 60 Muslim men in Zaklopaca --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: You're kindly requested to read slower for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- and you also agreed that the IPTF concluded that Milomir Milosevic from the Milici SJB had a role in the massacre and that he was suspended from service as a result. You recall saying that in the Krajisnik case, do you is not? Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bad translation. IPTF then suspected him of having taken part. However, after that when the investigation was carried out completely the man proved to be absolutely innocent, and in this last judgement the Government of Republika Srpska has to return him to the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, you have spent so far an hour and 40 minutes about. How much longer do you need?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would need at least a half an hour to deal with the Srebrenica matters, possibly 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, the Chamber would like you to conclude by the end of this session, in half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, I now want to turn your attention to 1995, when you were president of the Municipal Assembly of Milici. At that time your telephone number was 741-028, was it not?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Which number of mine are you referring to, actually?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 24608A, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You had a colleague in Milici named Milos Lalovic. Do you recall his telephone number, 741-016?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milos Lalovic? I don't think there's any such person in Lalovici. There are quite a few Lalovics, but not a Milos Lalovic. I wouldn't know who Milos Lalovic is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mile. Mile Lalovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mile.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, Mile Lalovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, you see on the screen here this is an extract from the MOD Zvornik district telephone directory. You see your name, president of the municipality, telephone number, and Mile Lalovic, president of the Executive Board, and his telephone number, 741-016. Do you recall now these telephone numbers?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I couldn't remember. Doesn't mean a thing to me. Well, it's possible that they're correct, I mean, but I don't remember. I do not remember that those were the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No foundation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You were, he said it may be possible that these numbers are -- are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But you only asked about the number, but you didn't ask a question about this document itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, do you see this extract from the Zvornik district telephone directory? Would there be any reason that these numbers -- we can presume that the numbers here are the numbers of yours and Mr. Lalovic's telephone numbers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Office numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, work numbers.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: None of these numbers mean a thing to me. I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have the entire document of this? You said it's an extract.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, 24608 is the entire document. Your Honour, I'm happy to move on if -- if -- due to the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. It's only of one page. Let's move on. You are not tendering this document -- or shall we mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We can mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI P6123, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you state that on the 11th of July, you received a report that the Muslim forces broke through the 1st Milici battalion at Bokcin Potok in order to cross the road at Kaldrmica and Zuberi. If we can first of all quickly have a map up on the screen 65 ter number 24608 to try and orient the Chamber to where these locations are that you mention in your statement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we need a different number.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: 24606. Thank you. While we are waiting for that map to come up, you said that there were many fatalities on both sides. Many Muslim fatalities? Mr. Savkic?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: How many Serb fatalities?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you said that this was parallel to or along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road, or the Milici-Konjevic Polje road. This is the area that you're talking about, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you say that this happened on the 11th of July, 1995, and you just recently corrected your statement to read 11 of July, not 11 or 12 July 1995. That's correct, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was the paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Paragraph 91.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Para number again, 91?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, 89.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The 11th of July, in the evening hours, yes, I did receive information that Muslim forces made the breakthrough, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the 11th of July is the day Srebrenica fell or was liberated. That's right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what you say, then that would be it. I am interested in my municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said that it was the head that broke through.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We know exactly which brigade, which commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, the Muslim column did not even reach this road and wasn't even close by the 11th of July, 1995. And if we could have -- first of all, if we can -- if you can look at this map, these areas, the Zuberi area, the Kaldrmica area, and the Mratinci area and the Buljin area are all areas that you have listed in your statement. Is this -- are these locations correctly put on this map? Mr. Savkic, you see this map in front of you. Does this accurately reflect where these positions are, these areas that you refer to in your statement? Is this map correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If it's not correct, can you please say what's not correct and take the marker, the pen there that you have. The usher will assist you. What are you saying is not correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zuberi, all of this that is displayed here. Here, this part. I beg your pardon. So all of this is Konjevic Polje. All of that is Konjevic Polje. Kaldrmica -- Kaldrmica is all of this Djugum area -- what is area --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Area. Djugum area.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this please be interpreted to the witness. And the word to be used should be "zona [phoen]" rather than "proster [phoen]."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpret's note: We did not hear the witness because of Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this is it, then -- just a moment, please. Then all of this -- I mean, if you're referring to these houses around Djun Kafana [phoen], well, that would be it. Well, the Bratunac area, well, I'd have to take a look. Kravica is a far broader notion. This is only the centre of Kravica. Sandici, well ... I would not say that this is Pervani, but Pervani is to the left. Well, all right. Tentatively, in terms of orientation, let's say that that would be it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I assist with the transcript. The interpreters did not hear that. The witness asked that -- to be told what "area" means. The interpreter said "proster." Since he is an officer, I think that it would be easier if it were translated as "zona" to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think he heard your intervention earlier on. Let's continue in any event. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, could you please just put a -- put a --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- KP up near the Zuberi area that you marked as the Konjevic Polje area. Put the initials KP and then please sign and date the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if I could tender that map then, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Konjevic, Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you please sign and date the map.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Today's the 15th?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, this Trial Chamber has evidence before it that -- and this is Exhibit P04939, that it was confirmed that a large group of Muslims left the Srebrenica area on the night between the 11th and 12th of July, 1995, which contradicts what you've said, that they were up in the Kaldrmica and Zuberi area by the 11th.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the 281st Brigade, well, actually this was my former battalion that had positions at Valjevo. They reported to me, and they said to me very nicely, I quote what I was told then from Bokcin Potok, and then further up towards Mratinci. Well, literally they said to me, "Everything's black."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, the -- the 11th of July, Drina Corps daily combat report which is -- we can bring that up. 65 ter number 2 -- 02002, indicates that no combat activity in the area of Konjevic Polje and Nova Kasaba. In fact, as you'll see when the report comes up, it indicates that the security in the Drina Corps zone of responsibility is good. It says that five VRS soldiers were killed on the 11th of July, 1995, but not in connection with any activity in the area of Konjevic Polje and Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement, well, I received information. I'm reading paragraph 81. On the 11th of July, 1995, I received information stating that Muslim forces had penetrated Bokcin Potok. These are the areas that you marked. This is 5 or 6 kilometres away. So that's not it. That's not what you asked about. And of course what is missing here is during the night they passed along the road in Kaldrmica. I mean, this is this man from Bratunac. He mentioned Zuberi but it's Konjevic Polje. It's that area and there was combat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. -- Mr. Savkic?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there were quite a few fatalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a regular combat report signed by Milenko Zivanovic, who was the Drina -- from the Drina Corps command staff, setting out what the position was on the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I take it you are tendering the marked map as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we give the number first?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the map is P6124.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And this one?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And this one will be Exhibit P6125.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And we have no reports indicating many fatalities on the 11th of July as you just testified to a moment ago on the VRS side, because there were virtually none on the VRS RS MUP side, and that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all of this is fine. This is a regular combat report of the Drina Corps in Bokcin Potok. Everybody knows that by now. In Bokcin Potok, when crossing over, the Muslim formations were not fighting with the Army of Republika Srpska. Rather, they were fighting between themselves, because communications were down, and everyone knows that. That's what wounded Muslims said. This is what our people saw. This was fighting that had been unseen before. This is the territory of Bokcin Potok. They're far away. So they were fighting between themselves there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, I'll show you some video footage shortly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Savkic, do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then let's continue then, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, we have Borovcanin's 10 to 20 July report which is Exhibit P04960 which -- excuse me a moment. Yes, in paragraph 89 of your statement you say that there were many fatalities on both sides, but in fact I've just taken you to documents which show that there were no fatalities on both sides, and that was in the document that we've just admitted. In Borovcanin's 10 to 20 July report it indicates and this is P4960, that in the -- it is only in the afternoon of the 12th of July that the MUP received information from state security that 12- to 15.000 able-bodied Muslims were moving from Srebrenica to Konjevic Polje. So on the 12th of July, there is no sign of a battle with heavy losses either, and the 12th of July VRS Main Staff daily report indicates that on that day in the Drina Corps zone only one VRS soldier was slightly wounded - and this is Exhibit P03054 - and that there were no fatalities on the Serb side. In fact, there were never heavy fatalities on the Serb side caused from the Muslims in the column until at the 16th at Baljkovica. To the contrary, on the 13th of July, the Serb forces started capturing thousands of Muslim civilians and soldiers from the column and thousands of men surrendered to the VRS and the MUP along the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje -- Konjevic Polje road; correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He has no idea. He has no idea. Information on the breakthrough of the Muslim forces, the first breakthrough on the 11th, I personally communicated that to Malinic down there at the Protection Regiment. The fist obstacle, well, the Muslims themselves say that. The first obstacle they had to cross was through minefields. A few antipersonnel mines exploded.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why don't you let me tell you what the truth is? He has no idea whatsoever. I'm going to tell you everything. I'm going to tell you the names of the casualties from my battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We'll have a break now and we'll give you ten minutes after the break. Mr. Savkic, you may be excused now. We'll continue after the short lunch break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland, why is the date that important? Whether it was 11th, 12th, or 13th, 16th in relation to this witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Because, Your Honour, basically this witness's evidence is -- is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. In terms of date. Yes, let's suppose he messed up the date. Then he's -- based on the -- that date, his entire testimony will be false. Is that your case or -- my question is whether the date has specific connotation or bearing upon his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If Your Honour would give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's the fact that the -- the date is incorrect. It's out by -- by two days. But also the fact that there was no Serb -- there was no Serb casualties to the extent that this witness is saying there is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, very well. Yes, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If 89 were to be read correctly, then we would see that after Bokcin Potok they crossed the road and that is only when there's a reference to Serb casualties, not before that. And it doesn't even have to be the 11th anymore, but on the 11th they were in Bokcin Potok. Then they crossed the road as they were fighting, and then there's a reference to casualties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's the matter to be seen. Very well. We'll have a break for 45 minutes and resume at 11 past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could the Chamber move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, I take it notification should be reclassified as confidential.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, I don't see anything in the notification that refers to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you see the associated exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Actually, the associated exhibit -- that annex has already and reclassified as confidential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. I note it. Please continue, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you said that Muslims "engaged in armed combat when crossing the road" and very many of them were killed and this is from paragraphs 89 to 90 of your statement. I want to show you a short video-clip of some video of the road on the 13th of July, 1995, and of the VRS MUP engagement with members of the column, and this is at Sandici. If we could please play the video. And I will go on to play the clip, Your Honours, from 00:30:50 to 00:31:55.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This Muslim man that you see in the video-clip, Ramo Mustafic, when he says, Of course I'm scared, he was found in a Srebrenica associated grave, and that's, for Your Honours' and Mr. Karadzic, P04642. Mr. Savkic, that was what was happening when the Muslims were crossing the road where -- where you say they were crossing in paragraphs 89 to 90.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you have shown us could be footage from just about anywhere and you can say it's in Sandici, but it has nothing to do with the part I indicated on the map where I said they went through to my municipality. I'll tell you this --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell you about what things looked like where I stopped.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, this was the Muslims surrendering at the creek destroyed white house, and this was from the Srebrenica trial video P04201.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, I'll play you quickly another clip then, and this is clip number 1, and it is also at Sandici from the same Srebrenica trial video from -- I wish to play 00:17:46 to 00:19:04.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You see, that was -- that was Sandici, wasn't it, the area that you saw on the video-clip?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we go back to the map, please, so that I can show you where this is and where the weapons were that I saw, and you'll see that there were no civilians. There were thousands upon thousands of pieces of weapons when I walked over that part.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, I'm moving on in the interests of time. If Mr. Karadzic wishes to do that in redirect, then he may wish to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You know Mane Djuric of the Zvornik MUP, don't you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: He was Dragomir Vasic's deputy in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps. I don't remember. It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I want to show you an excerpt from his diary. If I can have 65 ter number 24067A, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It wasn't released, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, while we're waiting just in materials of expiration of the time, I would just point out that the playing of these video-clips didn't really advance much that couldn't have been advanced through a closing submission. So when you're considering how much time, and particularly the fact that we have one more witness who would like to finish today, I think I'd ask you to keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm very sorry, but I can't restrain myself from responding to that. The witness testified that on this time, and we got the dates straight, that there was heavy combat on the road on both sides in this area which we say is this area. That is why the video played. I don't tell my friend how to do his directs or his crosses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's proceed. Thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm advised that it has been released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we are seeing that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could just scroll so that we have the top of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, this is from the 14th of July, 1995, and we see at the top right-hand corner it has the Vlasenica number of your colleague, Mile Lalovic, 741-016. And underneath it also has Tomo, and we can see on the B/C/S that there's an initial below the Tomo. Mane Djuric says that this refers to you in his interview on the 21st of June, 2010. Who else is in this entry with you? Directly under your name there's another number, and who's -- what's the name underneath that? Popovic? Do you see it on the top right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that would be Vujadin Popovic; right, the 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Radovan Popovic in our unit. He's a civil engineer. He was employed in the mine, if that's the Popovic I have in mind. Radovan Popovic whose brother Kojo Popovic had been taken to Srebrenica and killed there like a stray dog. It's good that you show this document. He was captured in Kravica on the 7th of January, 1993, taken to Srebrenica and killed like a stray dog.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You see the number between your name and Popovic's name. That's the phone number of a house in Orahovac across from the school.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it's the Prosecution's case that this house and number was used by the VRS security organ in Orahovac, i.e., Popovic. Mr. Savkic, Mane Djuric puts you in this same conversation with Popovic with the 4th Battalion and the security organs house used in Orahovac, and on that same day, the 14th of July, 1995, that Popovic and the 4th Battalion are executing over a thousand men in Orahovac. So it's referencing to Vujadin Popovic not Dragan Popovic that you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Dragan but Radovan. I say it can be any Popovic. That last name doesn't mean anything much. All of this scribble, I don't know why this is being shown. There are no telephone conversation -- conversations during that time, and there's no date. It doesn't mean anything to me. I know exactly what I did, where I was. So, yeah, I understand you, but this has got nothing to do with me. No way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this, mark it for identification at the very least.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. It's not relevant. I would like to know if it's the Prosecution's case that Mr. Savkic participated in any of these executions. That's the implication here. I actually have my own notes in which I have different people's names and different things on the same piece of paper. So I don't think that this is even in any way relevant unless the Prosecution intends to assert that Mr. Savkic had something to do with the activities of Vujadin Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm -- sorry, we will seek to tender this document through another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. But I note that the telephone number and witness's -- witness's name was written in different pen, but it's for you to tender it later. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any re-examination, Mr. Karadzic, for this witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just have to, your Excellency. Such extensive cross-examination deserves some explanation by the witness. I will start with the most recent topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Savkic, please look at paragraph 89 of your statement. Can you tell us where, how, and then which of these locations the soldiers of the 128th Division of the Army of BH came into combat contact with the VRS? Was it at Bokcin Potok?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can be precise if I were shown that map, since until the 1st of November, 1993, I commanded that battalion. So the position of my battalion was from Buljin towards Derventa. And because at that point in time I did not have a left-hand side neighbouring unit, our lines were curved and went towards Mratinci, which is beyond Bokcin Potok. Why do I refer to that? Two of our trenches, since the Drinjaca company didn't dare or couldn't be at that side because then they would be left without their left neighbouring unit too, I allowed for two of our trenches to be moved so that the first and the second trench would be manned by the Drinjaca company. They had just broken through between the two trenches of ours on the left side towards the Drinjaca company and in the direction of the rest battalion which was at their positions near Buljin. I told you they had first gone through a quadruple minefield. There were two minefields of tripwire mines and two minefields of antipersonnel bombs, and of course that couldn't have gone unnoticed because many of them went off. 121st Brigade went through the first, and when the end of our positions from the battalion at Mratinci saw them, they probably opened fire and there was chaos because one part of the brigade had already gone through. There were others coming on as well, and they probably lost communication. There was an exchange of fire between the end position of our battalion, which may have interrupted all sorts of communication between the two parts of that brigade. It is not in dispute that the two brigades basically fought each other the whole night in that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see 24606 so that Mr. Savkic's officer can mark it. We'll also need it for -- because of Sandici. 24606. Did you have casualties when the first contact was established near the trenches?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Two fighters. There were so many of them that two of our soldiers were in a dugout, and they just picked them up along the way. They took them alive and to date we or I at least have not been able to find out what happened with them. One of them was called Jankovic, and he was the cousin of Pajlot Jankovic. There was another one, Ljubisa Jovanovic, who hailed from Kravica. That's why I was quite upset last time to see in a document that there was no fighting whatsoever. They simply, once they arrived, took both of them alive. So they were the first casualties. That was on that day when they were breaking through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They were captured --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Is this what you heard or what you saw, Mr. Savkic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard it by -- from some people who told me as the municipal president. Everyone knows about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I can direct your attention at P4496, item 7, losses or casualties. The 1st Milici Infantry Brigade during the day at around 3.00 p.m. two fighters had gone missing during search of the terrain in the Potok area, the two soldiers being Jovanovic and Ratko.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpret's note: Mr. Karadzic read that out too fast and the speakers are overlapping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Could you give the number again and put -- and pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, if I might interrupt. And this is redirect so if Mr. Karadzic can lay a foundation and ask a question before he puts a document to the witness and doesn't ask questions in leading form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that my learned friend Ms. Sutherland disputed Mr. Savkic's statement that there were casualties on the Serb side and he wasn't allowed to tell the names of the people who were the initial casualties at Bokcin Potok. Before I read out the names to him, he told -- he said the names himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I didn't dispute that there were casualties on the Serb side. I in fact led in my questions to Mr. Savkic that there were, I think I said five Serb casualties, and I read -- referring to the exhibit. So that is not correct, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us this: Were these two ever returned?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. Even today we still don't know anything about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They were not identified in any graves?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have such information. It may be possible that they were found in some Muslim graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 4450, there's also a reference to five killed and three wounded?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic. Mr. Karadzic, you heard the objection of Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am trying to confirm what Ms. Sutherland said a moment ago where she stated that she mentioned five victims. However, these five are different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, can you tell us this looking at the paragraph: What happened next -- sorry, before that? Before they crossed the road at Kaldrmica and Konjevic Polje, were Muslim soldiers being killed and how? In what way?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first there was an exchange of fire with the 1st Milici Battalion. Next, the company that was nearby also opened fire. I presume that was the Drinjaca Company. And the biggest clash for the Serb side as well took place between the Muslim units at Gornji Bratinci [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we assist Mr. Savkic with a pen so to indicate -- to indicate where the minefields were, where the Serbs engaged Muslims, and where the Muslims fought between themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me for interrupting again but can Mr. Karadzic establish from the witness whether this is something that the witness knows because he was there or because he heard it and if so if he heard it, who did he hear it from. At the moment it's sounding like the witness is right there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's the point of my question. Let's continue, and then could you put that to the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, where was your unit deployed on this map?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this map my unit -- well, like this. Ravni Buljin, and then this is the part I talked about, which went like this. Then near Brezani, further on. The line stopped around here. There was a reserve platoon which was in Dolovi village. Here it is. Near the school building. There was a reserve platoon there with some guys who were better. This part towards Tuzla was open throughout the period, and from Buljin it went towards Derventa and the settlement on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you just mark the direction of Derventa with a D?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Next to the line itself can you write the Milici battalion or Milici Brigade, MB?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Milici battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you have a unit of yours in Sandici?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. That area did not have any military units at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you circle the area where the Muslims were killed in a minefield and how many.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. I'll tell you exactly. This is a slope, and our minefields were placed like this and then like this. Just give me a moment to get my bearings. So there was one section of a minefield particularly planted with antipersonnel mines. Now, somewhere here were the two trenches of the Milici battalion, and then this was the line held by the Drinjaca Company. So that was the situation. Therefore, they first came across Bokcin Potok, which I marked. They passed through this area and then went on along this line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please. Please mark the minefield with letters MF.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] This is a bit slanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark Bokcin Potok with BP.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] Then it says here --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us did you see this with your own eyes or were you informed about the events by your unit about how many people were killed, how many pieces of weapons that were discarded you found, et cetera. Tell us all of this.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, the initial information I received from my troops. They phoned me, and since this is a forestry area, it's difficult to see the dead in the minefield, but one could hear the mines going off. So sometime after the 15th of July, I don't know exactly when, and a couple of other men went and toured this entire area where my battalion was deployed. I don't know if I should draw it, the direction which we took.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's not important where you went, but tell me what you found out and in what manner.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw everything with my own eyes. Within this circle, particularly here --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I don't think this arises from my cross-examination, this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You challenged the witness with witnessing --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: On the date and massive casualties on the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you not challenge the witness' witnessing Muslim corpses, albeit indirectly? I will consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was -- I was cross-examining him about the fact that there was no heavy armed conflict when they were crossing the road and the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, we shall like very much to hear you reply to Ms. Sutherland's submission on this matter, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Judge Baird. I was just wondering myself if I was misunderstanding the Prosecution's position, because it was my understanding that their cross-examination was trying to show that this event that the witness described, including thousands and hundreds of bodies of Muslims who died either in combat with the Serbs or in combat with each other, I thought that they were -- the point of their cross-examination was to show that this event did not take place, and if I'm mistaken in that and if they agree that it took place in the way that the witness said it, then perhaps there's no need for redirect, but I suspect that that's not the case and I think it falls squarely within the cross-examination if that's the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll allow the accused to continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So as briefly as possible and accurately as possible. Where did you see this number of corpses, and how had they died? How did these soldiers die? Tell us everything. How many died in the minefield, how many died in Mratinci, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only in the circle of Mratinci, when the four of us were going through, we saw bodies next to each other, and the area toward Bokcin Potok is forested, and on the other side you have meadows, this slope, and you can see downwards. At that time when I was there, the bodies were swollen, which led me to believe that that was after the 15th, and there were already maggots appearing and I'm sure that the forensic can confirm that they died two days prior to that date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you say this, can you please use the pencil and indicate what you're showing, because otherwise we don't know.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the area that I'm talking about. This is above Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How did they die?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these men, as far as I could observe, were mostly killed by gunshot wounds, by bullets. In this forested area and towards the peak, there were dead bodies whose abdomens were blown as a result of being shot by an LPG of the Chinese make, and there were at least a hundred of them scattered around and nobody collected them. Now, another interesting thing, below the red line towards the forested area, the majority of fighters were facing the stream - I'm talking about the dead bodies - whilst others up there were facing or turned towards Mratinci village. Gornji Mratinci village. I didn't go to the area on the left, but I think it's obvious to everyone here that the fighting took place towards Bokcin Potok and that there was also fighting towards Gornji Mratinci where our troops were not deployed. It is possible that this platoon had reached the end of the positions of our battalions and that they got killed in clashes with that platoon. But as I said, there was so many dead bodies you could hardly avoid treading on them. Later on, before I arrived, all automatic and semi-automatic weapons were collected --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The question was how did they die. The witness said all these men as far as I could observe were mostly killed by gunshot wounds. That's the answer. And the witness has gone on now for three paragraphs. The other thing I would note, Your Honour, is this map. He's drawn a circle within this Mratinci area. I don't know whether Your Honours want him to do a notation for what this circle represents so that the record's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Who made the circle?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The witness just drew the red circle within the larger black circle on the map in front of us, but I don't know whether he needs to put what in fact that circle represents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Savkic --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The red circle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What does the red circle mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The red circle indicates the largest number of dead Muslim bodies and an area where the weapons that belonged to the dead men remained, the weapons that hadn't been driven away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please put STB or SDB which stands for concentration of dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside of the circle. So since this is where the two men, our two men who were taken away and this area indicates where they were passing through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How many bodies were in minefields?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't dare go over there, because these minefields were partly constructed whilst I was a commander, and after that engineering units from Pale were involved. So I didn't go there. One can only assume, and according to the stories I heard from my men, there were bodies there because in actual fact they entered between the Milici battalion and the Drinjaca Company. They passed through that area. I didn't see those bodies, but I heard that were quite a few of them. So this part between the Drinjaca Company positions and this one here. I'm talking about what I saw. But I did hear that the situation was the same there in this entire area of Pobudje. People were telling me that there were numberless dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please indicate the place where the Drinjaca Company was deployed with letters DK.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So from here I will just put an arrow, because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me briefly how many pieces of weapons were discarded by those who were either killed or who surrendered? You said that in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A truckload full of weapons FAP was loaded with the weapons collected there, as well as two tractor loads of weapons who were taken to the Milici Brigade. While I was passing through the area, I could see M-48 rifles, submachine-guns, M-53, hunting rifles, and also LPGs of the Chinese make which I mentioned earlier with all these rockets, and there were bodies. I said that along this line which I marked, I saw at least 100 LPGs, and that stands for light rocket launchers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that they were killed by the Chinese LPG. Did we have this kind of weapon in our arsenal?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, we didn't have that kind of weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Less distinguish what you saw and what you heard first. What is it that you saw, Mr. Savkic, at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I saw LPGs, which stands for light rocket launchers of the Chinese make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw rifles M-48.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry. Please tell us again what you saw. Including the bodies, weapons or whatever. Tell us all that you saw at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Weapons, dead bodies, a car, Zastava 285. This is probably the Zepa Brigade. I saw back-packs and other sacks full of ammunition, 762-millimetre automatic and semiautomatic rifles. Well, that would be all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This entire area that I encircled. And I can also show you down there where I went from Kamenica downwards along the road to Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark it on the map, because we can't see it.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I went down this road. I think this is how it runs from Kamenica. [Marks]. At any rate, we were coming from that direction when we had battalion rotation. We would hit the main road and then go back towards Konjevic Polje and this here. Of course there were dead bodies on this section of the road as well but far fewer than on this part up there marked C, D, B, or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you mark the road with letter R or P.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only write Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So put a P.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just one more question. Do you know what happened with these bodies? Have any sanitation measures been undertaken, and where were they buried? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have official information which came out in July 1998. I was the president of the Milici Municipal Assembly. A representative of the International Red Cross told me that from this area, but not only from the area that I marked, but from the area -- from the Konjevic Polje road all the way to Pobudje the commission, which I later heard whose commission it was, collected 2.600 Muslim skeletons and that they were taken to the old part of the Lipnica mine. I have her photograph. Her name was Ines Miska [phoen], I think. So it's not a problem. Anyway, it is common knowledge. The local Muslims and Serbs were involved in collecting these bones from that area. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. One more question with regard to the map. Could you please use a blue pencil and mark the direction that they took in order to cross the area of Pobudje and where they crossed the road and the river Jadar.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to have this map lowered a bit. I forgot to mention that this whole road from Gornji Mratinci all the way to Kamenica which I took, that was something very striking that I will never forget. The part of the column that was crossing the meadows 5 to 6 metres on the average, it looked like an asphalt road. There was not a single grass -- grass blade left intact. Now I'm using the blue pencil, and this is the road that we are talking about and what I saw as they were passing. So this is the section that I discussed. [Marks]. Maybe a bit to the left, but as I said, the width was 5 to 6 metres where they passed, and they trod on the grass. If you go along this slope, you can reach Pobudje, but we need to move the map to see Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If we do that, we're going to lose everything, and it's not necessary. Just put the date and your initials in the lower right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, could this be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Two questions, Mr. Savkic. How do you know that Muslim column followed that blue route?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I explained to you a while ago. If you look at this blue circle, I told you nicely. In this area, when they went out, the grass was trodden in the width of 5 to 6 metres on the average. There was not a single grass blade left. It was just dirt, black earth, and peasant shoes cannot easily eliminate grass. And also a civilian footwear cannot do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How did you know that some of them were killed by Chinese LPG?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They could have been killed by bombs, by the Chinese LPGs. This is an assumption. Maybe they were killed by rifle grenades, but if you see such huge wounds, these are not bullet wounds. So everybody knows that, and I suppose I was someone who had an opportunity to see my own men killed by grenades, my men from my battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: On several occasions you said "my troops" or "my battalion." Were you in a military hierarchical position at the time in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. As of 1st November, 1993, I didn't have any military position. However, I don't know the War Presidency of the municipality to be a military position. But as far as command structure is concerned, I held no post whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive this marked map as next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D2941, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, today you were asked about Zaklopaca. That was on page 56 of today's transcript, and paragraphs 63 through 65 of your statement. You were asked -- or, rather, it was suggested that it was not true that this had not been planned and prepared, and you were asked about Serb casualties. Were those all civilians, Mr. Savkic, and was Zaklopaca a place that had its own armed group that used to go -- become engaged in fighting and then come back?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Speaking about Zaklopaca, before the events there took place there is no doubt that it is true that Muslims of Zaklopaca said at the public security station, although some of them returned with weapons, but the others told them what kind of weapons certain individuals had in their possession, and they enumerated those weapons. They also said that there was a group of some 30 men that when war operations began between Derventa, Rudnik, Milici, Skelani, took part alongside paramilitary formations, TO Djile. So there is no doubt about that. This is what the Muslims said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have 1D4124, and I apologise for this not having been translated, because I never anticipated this to be in dispute. So 1D4124.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can Mr. Karadzic please be cautioned not to ask leading questions and also to lay a foundation before he puts the document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm doing my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But I wanted to ask you, sir, Mr. Savkic, do you know what Zalisine is?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe I laid a foundation through my previous question. Could I ask you to read this document, and could you please tell us with a this document is.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to answer. Well, you see, this is a report of the 1st Zepa Brigade, and it is providing information to the 2nd Corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it is stated clearly that the above-mentioned persons were killed in Zaklopaca after returning from Zalisine. Zalisine was the headquarters with Ravno Gora, the headquarters of the TO of Djile, and that was commanded by Fadil Turkovic. So this is confirmation of what I said earlier on, namely that one of these formations out of 30 took part in the operations from the 1st of May until the 7th of May, 1992, in all of those things that were happening in that area.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all other microphone please be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please read the first paragraph. Could you finish reading this paragraph. There are names up there.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes: "Could you please provide information for us for Muradif Hreljic, born 1960, in Zaklopaca, municipality of Vlasenica, and Murat Hreljic born in 1963, in Zaklopaca, municipality of Vlasenica."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The above-mentioned persons were killed in Zaklopaca upon returning from Zalisine on the 16th of May, 1992, and they were members of the unit of Fadil Turkovic. We are sending this information on the basis of the statement made by the parent (father) Osman Hreljic."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the benefit of the participants, may I say that Murat Hreljic is registered in P4282, Amor Masovic's findings as a victim of an execution. Can this be admitted, page 57 in that exhibit, referred to as an execution victim or, rather, a person who had been killed. Actually, identified in a mass grave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D2942, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, you mentioned Djile a moment ago. Can you tell us why Djile is important and what happened there?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Djile is very important, because after a deep canyon in front of Djile - I mean there's Djile - and then behind Djile is the bauxite mine. Sometime towards the end of the month of September 1991, Ibrahim Ademovic nickname Sakura, together with another group of persons who were similar to him and with an M-56 automatic weapon stopped buses that transported the Boksit workers, and he sent them to Milici on foot from there. When the police patrol came, well, that's how he behaved the first time, September --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. How does this arise out of cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has to do with Zaklopaca, your Excellency. Would I prefer a shorter answer, but it does have to do with Zaklopaca. I'm interested in the importance of Djile that is mentioned in the document and the importance of Derventa. Very briefly, and we have received an answer as to what Zalisine is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Djile is the headquarters of the battalion -- or, rather, the Territorial Defence detachment. At that moment this is a parallel paraformation. So that is the headquarters of this detachment, and it was named after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you just tell us why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Pause. Pause. Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why is Derventa important?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Derventa is important -- well, from Derventa towards the mine there is this road that goes through Muslim villages, and what is important is that in Derventa, at the end of April and the beginning of May, about 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Karadzic, I can't follow the line of questioning. Why it is important to the witness has nothing to do with us. So how does it arise from the cross-examination of Ms. Sutherland? You put specific question and lay foundation and you may put some documents or other propositions, but why certain thing is important to witness has nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Excellencies. Perhaps my questions were not skilful enough, but all of these are locations where heavy fighting took place, but I shall move on. And now I'd like to call up the following document 1D4073, and while we're waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know Mustafa Mehmedovic or have you heard of him? He's from Zaklopaca.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mahmutovic. That's a mistake. Mahmutovic Mustafa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have that document? Do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about that later, that he lost his life in Zaklopaca. And I knew about him beforehand. Before the war he was armed with two automatic weapons. He returned one, and that is his statement. And the other one he kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you confirm that what is being proposed here is that he -- or, rather, that these persons received decorations? So can we see bottom part of the page. It's the Muslim committee for commemorating some anniversary or other, and the names of different fighters are listed there, those who had been proposed for decorations. Can we have the next page now. The next page, please. And now the bottom of the payment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, how does this arise from cross-examination? I specifically cross-examined in relation to Zaklopaca about the incident that happened on the 16th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it that Mahmutovic was one of the victims killed on that day. Otherwise, I'd like to ask --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But the witness has actually confirmed that he said that this gentleman died in the Zaklopaca incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And then whether there was -- he was killed as a -- as plan as you put it in your cross or whether he was killed during the combat. I think he's entitled to --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I agree. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I then ask you to read what this says, why he is being proposed for a decoration posthumously. Does -- the part that is underlined.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He thoroughly prepared for the war having bought two weapons, and he particular --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. But before we proceed, let's identify what -- who we are talking about. This document -- this document is talking about Mehmetovic, Mehmedovic, but you said Mahmutovic. Who are we talking about, Mr. Karadzic? Let's clarify that first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us what his last name was and whether this is the man that is being referred to here?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very easy to establish. It's just the last name where the mistake was made. His name, the name of his father, where he was born, when he was born, father's name, mother's name, all of it fits except Mahmutovic, this Ibro Nuhanovic wrote Mehmedovic, or perhaps it was just a typo. It was probably handwritten and somebody was typing this up and that's where the mistake was made and all the rest can be established easily. Then there are the victims of Zaklopaca who lost their lives there, so it's no problem. Everything else fits. So it's not Mehmedovic but it's Mahmutovic. All the rest is -- corresponds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The witness just spoke of this -- what the witness just said now, we can find that in Amor Masovic's report.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mahmut Fezim Mustafa [phoen], and all the other information except that the last name is?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Right there, wrong here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's nothing to do with your re-examination of this witness. That's subject of your further submissions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like the witness to read why it is that they made this proposal to decorate this man who got killed in this incident in Zaklopaca. Why they wanted to confer decoration upon him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was preparing for war thoroughly. Having bought two weapons, and he particularly figured prominently in organising the people of Zaklopaca for were resisting the aggressor. During the first half of May, the above mentioned person established a unit consisting of about 30 armed neighbours and moved to the nearby mountain of Birac with them with the intention of linking up --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the same formation from the area of Derventa.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be zoomed in a bit for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And could you please go on reading.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because -- well, this is probably a typo again, because the Derventa unit did not carry out what had been agreed upon. There was hesitation in Mustafa's unit, and the members of the unit decided to return to the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please go on. The entire section that has been circled, but please read it slowly so that it can be interpreted.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander warned of the danger involved because of the total encirclement, because the area was totally encircled by Serb population. He remained isolated in terms of such thinking because he said that he did not want to stay as an exception if he is going to return to a hornet's nest. Unfortunately, his assumptions turned out to be the bitter truth, and the fatal mistake in the assessment of his neighbours resulted in a genocide. That was the consequence. Genocide over -- over 60 inhabitants of this hamlet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who is proposing that he be decorated?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the SDA of Vlasenica headquartered in Srebrenica, Ibro Nuhanovic with a degree of economics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There are other members of the commission, too; right?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from all these municipalities, Srebrenica, Bratunac, Zvornik and Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said to us today that people were furious. They came because some of their people had been killed and their suspicion was that their soldiers who got killed had been fired at from that village. What do you say to that now? Was this well founded, this suspicion of these persons who had killed them returning to Zaklopaca?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That day part of the column, part of a JNA column passed through Vlasenica, and they had been victimised in Tuzla on the previous day. In addition to that, a column from the Motorised Brigade from Jastrebarsko, from Croatia, was also passing by. It is beyond dispute that on that day, our entire unit, that is to say that battalion, was involved in heavy combat with the units from Srebrenica and Zepa in the area between Derventa and the canyon facing the mine. The police was there too, and they were supposed to secure that road once the enemy was driven away. They were supposed to secure that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, can this be admitted for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D2943.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, Mr. Karadzic, you referred to Mr. Masovic's report or Exhibit as P4282. Could you give me the correct number?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The correct number is P, so it's a Prosecution number, 4852. And the page is 57 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll change topics now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I wanted to go back to the beginning of the cross-examination. Mr. Savkic, you were asked why you did not list the positions you had within your party when you created the list of your official positions. Can you tell us what was it that you omitted and why? Can you tell us what sort of positions you were appointed to in your area, in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my municipality? You mean Milici or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: First Vlasenica and then Milici.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So as of November 1991, I think, until let's say the 31st -- well, I was never removed or dismissed, but until the Municipal Assembly of Milici was established. In that period, I was the president of the Municipal Board of the SDS in Vlasenica. In Milici, since war operations were already under way and I didn't have any similar function during the war. Later on when this body resumed its work, another person was appointed as its president because we didn't have enough time to do anything else. As I said, I became commander on the 1st of November, 1992. Before that, since I was a reserve military officer, for a while when I no longer worked in the bauxite mine, I was someone who provided engineering support, be it in securing the passage of JNA units or providing engineering support to the work of the mine or of certain Serb villages. I became president -- oh, yes. In the meantime, no one asked about it, when Goran Zekic, a member of parliament, was killed, I became a deputy in the RS Assembly. When the War Presidency was established in 1991, it was established, but as we can see in the documents, the Municipal Assembly and the Executive Board of Milici municipality existed in parallel. So with the exception of that letter or document sent to the command of a unit, the War Presidency did not have any role to play. There was no need in Milici municipality, not before the 28th Division broke through the territory of Milici municipality. Well, if there's anything that I have forgotten, they can ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us this please: The bodies that were proclaimed or established, were they included in the -- among the authorities? Were they in power, as a matter of fact?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They never had any power, because they were unsuccessful in being constituted, and initially they even couldn't agree on the seat of the Autonomous Region of Birac. I just saw it here. They held one or two sessions where they elected people to some commissions or working bodies, and as far as I know, that was the last thing they did, unfortunately, and that is why we had gone through everything we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what were the reasons to forge those documents in 1998? What lay behind it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have explained it in detail last time. I said clearly certain companies on the instructions of the RS government, when those instructions referred to the functioning of the Crisis Staffs, well, in those instructions the tasks of Crisis Staffs were specified. Among other things, it was stated that when the -- when the Municipal Assembly and Executive Board could not function, they could make decisions about state taxes so that such taxes be paid into the giro accounts of municipalities. Now, when in late -- well, at the end of that year, when the government asked to have the calculations made concerning funds, and to have them audited, it was discovered that the money didn't go to the municipal account but actually they went to the accounts of a company. When they tried to audit that information in Milici, attempts were made to do something that would go directly against the state. So in keeping with the instructions of the RS government, an attempt was made to create that document as if a decision had been made. They tried to serve that decision on me, and there was no rectangular stamp of the Municipal Assembly. There was only the protocol stamp of the bauxite company in Milici. I don't know where this one came from, but I could see it during the Krajisnik trial. So it was a reception stamp of the bauxite mine. I refused, of course, and it went unsigned. Later on when I refused, the managers of the company and certain people from the Municipal Assembly, including Mile Lalovic, did what they did. The bauxite company in late 1992 sorted out the disputed tax amounts with the RS government. I have that among my documents too. I have shown it here. So the figures seemed to tally and it turned out according to that that the Milici municipal revenue that went to the state was far greater than it really was. I didn't want any part of it. In all those documents you can see that they are not contemporaneous. Whatever document you pick up, you'll see that the municipal stamp at the time looked different. The stamp that was used here was probably created based on the stamp of the Municipal Assembly speaker in Milici in 1992. It's just that instead of "Republika Srpska" one can read the "Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." I'm not particularly interested in what those people did, and for some personal reasons or disagreements with certain people I'd rather not discuss it any further. It's a settled matter in my book. It's long gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would have several brief questions, but I will drop them. Thank you for having come and testified on behalf of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, that concludes your evidence, Mr. Savkic. On behalf the Chamber, I thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you're free to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll rise all together.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just make a correction to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: At transcript page 73, line 4, I gave an incorrect 65 ter number for the excerpt of Mane Djuric's diary. I said -- the proper number is 24607A. So even though it wasn't admitted, just so that the record is clear that that's the document I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And on another note, in relation to those two Birac documents, they have both been admitted in a previous trial, that was 65 ter number 17438A and 17442.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll note that. We'll continue next week on Monday. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 18th day of February, 2013, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
